name: Camera pull-back
one_line: The view widens from a detail to reveal the whole, placing the part in context
summary: The frame starts on a small detail and widens until the whole it belongs to comes into view, so the part is understood in context. It suits a closing reveal of scale or a diagram's full structure. Fast or full-frame moves can unsettle viewers, so it works best short, motivated and ending in a steady hold.

routes.one_line: Scale and translate a grouped SVG scene with Anime.js to widen the view

steps.does: Tween the scene group's scale and position from the detail to the whole
Seek, settle and screenshot each frame of the page

limits: Evidence covers a transform tween on a square, not a scale of a whole scene
Strokes and text scale with the group, so fine detail can soften at the closest view

routes.one_line: Move a Three.js camera back from the detail, rendered once per seek

steps.does: Position and frame the camera as a function of t, rendering each seek
Seek, settle and screenshot each frame of the page

limits: Three.js evidence is one static-camera scene in a Linux container with a stand-in Chromium
Camera moves are named in the tool's use but no fixture here is a pull-back

routes.one_line: Redraw a 2D canvas scene under a scale and offset that widen with t

steps.does: Apply a view scale and offset from t and redraw the whole scene

limits: Evidence is at device pixel ratio 1; resampling softness at large scale changes is untested
Detail is rasterised at one resolution, so the closest view may look soft unless drawn large

source: references/motion-director §6, references/accessibility §2.2; tool records as of 2026-11-20
